papers.title: Accelerating RLHF Training with Reward Variance Increase
papers.summary: Abstract. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is an essential technique for ensuring that large language models (LLMs) are aligned with human values and preferences during the posttraining phase. As an effective RLHF approach, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated success in many LLM-based applications. However, efficient GRPO-based RLHF training remains a challenge. papers.title: Vehicle adaptive cruise control based on safety constraints and continuous action surface reconstruction: An improved Q-learning method
papers.summary: The heavy vehicle mass and long braking delay mean that any following distance violation may lead to a serious rear-end collision. Although reinforcement learning has self-learning potential, it tends to output dangerous actions due to blind exploration during the early training stage. Moreover, the “cross gear jump” caused by discrete state spaces leads to abrupt acceleration changes, impairing ride comfort and drivetrain life. papers.title: Uncovering Latent Phase Structures and Branching Logic in Locomotion Policies: A Case Study on HalfCheetah
papers.summary: In locomotion control tasks, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated high performance; however, the decision-making process of the learned policy remains a black box, making it difficult for humans to understand. On the other hand, in periodic motions such as walking, it is well known that implicit motion phases exist, such as the stance phase and the swing phase. Focusing on this point, this study hypothesizes that a policy trained for locomotion control may also represent a phase structure that is interpretable by humans. papers.title: Correcting misconceptions and shaping preferences about energy with reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Addressing the climate crisis requires citizens to make informed choices about sustainable energy policy, yet public debates are often shaped by inaccurate beliefs about the environmental and health impacts of different energy sources. Misconceptions about key features of energy sources, such as their greenhouse gas emissions, mortality rates, and contribution to electricity production, are particularly dangerous for this debate, as they risk systematically distorting public support for effective decarbonisation strategies. papers.title: Unsupervised reward-driven image segmentation in automated scanning transmission electron microscopy experiments
papers.summary: Automated experiments in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) require rapid image segmentation to optimize the data representation for human interpretation, decision-making, site-selective spectroscopy, and atomic manipulation. Currently, segmentation tasks are typically performed using supervised machine learning methods, which require human-labeled data and are sensitive to out-of-distribution drift effects caused by changes in resolution, sampling, or beam shape. papers.title: RFAmpDesigner: A Two-Level LLM-guided Optimization Framework for Automated Differential CMOS RF Amplifier Sizing
papers.summary: Automated RF amplifier sizing is challenging because the design process is inherently hierarchical, the parameter space is high-dimensional and strongly coupled, and high-fidelity circuit simulation is expensive. Conventional optimization and reinforcement learning methods typically require many iterations and make limited use of RF domain knowledge, making them costly under tight simulation budgets. papers.title: The Everyday Life of Culture: Knowledge Transmission and Continuity in Indigenous and Adivasi Communities of South India
papers.summary: This article explores the transmission of traditional, ecological, cosmological, and social knowledge between the Kāṭṭu Nāyakar, Yerukala, and Irula communities of southern India. It argues that day-to-day activities such as domestic work, subsistence agriculture, divination, ritual, games and seasonal mobility constitute a structured learning ecology in which knowledge is learned through embodied participation rather than formal education. papers.title: Exploration Optimization for Dynamic Assortment Personalization under Linear Preferences
papers.summary: We study dynamic assortment personalization, where an online retailer adaptively selects assortments based on customer attributes to learn preferences and maximize revenue. We assume that product utilities depend linearly on customer attributes through an unknown coefficient matrix, leading to an exploration–exploitation trade-off. papers.title: Intellectual Tenacity at Work: Generative AI Exposure and the Economic Returns to Occupational Personality Requirements

papers.summary: Middle and secondary school educators should utilize and implement Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a support tool for instruction, not a replacement for their pedagogy and lesson planning. Utilizing and implementing AI can assist with lesson planning, differentiation, feedback, and generating learning materials; its uses should be guided by clear expectations, professional judgment, and school policy. papers.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning-Based Vehicle Localization for Both Urban Roads and GPS-Denied Environments
papers.summary: Accurate vehicle localization is critical for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, in GPS-denied environments such as tunnels or urban canyons, localization accuracy significantly deteriorates due to poor GPS signal quality. Traditional methods, such as extended Kalman filtering (EKF) and map matching, face limitations: EKF struggles with system nonlinearity and noise model assumptions, while map matching relies heavily on high-definition (HD) maps and often suffers in complex environments. papers.title: A surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning framework for layout optimization and economic assessment of dense urban vertical-axis wind turbine arrays
papers.summary: Urban wind energy is limited by space constraints and wake losses in dense arrays. This study integrates CFD-informed surrogate modelling with reinforcement learning to optimize compact vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) layouts. A three-stage clustering method reduces 82,103 complete hourly records from Winnipeg (2016–2025) to four representative speed states. papers.title: Data and code for Social Reinforcement Learning Drives Near-optimal Investment Patterns in Networked Best-Shot Games
papers.summary: This dataset accompanies the study "Social Reinforcement Learning Drives Near-optimal Investment Patterns in Networked Best-Shot Games". It provides simulation data and code for studying reinforcement learning and investment patterns in networked best-shot games on periodic lattices and Watts–Strogatz, Barabási–Albert, and Erdős–Rényi networks. The files are organized by manuscript figure. File descriptions, model parameters, data provenance, and reproduction instructions are provided in README.md.

Fraud detection was used as independent variable while Artificial intelligence was used as the independent variable. The determinants of artificial intelligence in this study will be automated chatbot, deep learning machine, machine learning solutions and natural language processing. papers.title: The energy module of FRIDA v2.1: endogenous investment and the timing of climate policy in the global energy system
papers.summary: Abstract. Integrated assessment models that derive energy-transition pathways from cost optimization or prescribed scenarios often diverge from observed investment behaviour. Here we present the energy module of FRIDA v2.1, a feedback-based, fully coupled global integrated assessment model built using System Dynamics, in which energy investment is endogenous. papers.title: Assessing the validity and reliability of computational phenotyping of motivation
papers.summary: Motivational disorders are a core clinical feature in neuropsychiatric disorders. The conventional method to assess motivation relies on clinical scales, however, an alternative approach is to use behavioral tasks, that can be combined with computational modelling. This is the so-called "computational phenotyping of motivation" approach. Nevertheless, if one wants to use computational phenotyping of motivation in longitudinal studies, it is crucial to assess the internal validity and the reliability of this approach. papers.title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
papers.summary: Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. papers.title: Multimodal private information and reward value shape information use during ant foraging
papers.summary: Animals use both private information acquired through experience and social information produced by conspecifics when making behavioural decisions. The combination of sensory cues and their associated reward value may influence how animals weigh private information against social information. We investigated information use during foraging in the ant Pristomyrmex punctatus using Y-maze experiments with learned visual and olfactory cues and trail pheromones. papers.summary: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) plays a central role in executive functions, including goal-directed behavior, working memory, cognitive flexibility, and decision-making, enabling individuals to adapt their actions to changing environmental demands. papers.title: AgriLemma in the Classroom: a Pilot Study for Game-Based Agricultural Education
papers.summary: Serious games designed for professional stakeholder projects rarely find use elsewhere and risk becoming redundant once the project ends. Education offers a natural second life for these games, bringing experiential learning into classrooms where students first encounter complex, real-world problems. papers.title: Youth policy as economic investment: Human capital, digital youth work and local development in the European Union
papers.summary: European youth policy is conventionally analysed through the lenses of participation, inclusion, citizenship, mobility and personal development. However, many of its instruments also generate effects that are economically significant, although they are not always captured by conventional measures of public expenditure efficiency. papers.title: A Generative AI Framework for Self-Learning and Autonomous Optimization in Cloud Infrastructure Management
papers.summary: The rapid evolution of cloud computing has intensified the need for intelligent, adaptive management systems capable of handling complex workloads, resource provisioning, and energy optimization autonomously.
